answer: To mint a fresh identity, an agent books one uniquely numbered hillside terrace for a single dawn and drives a uniquely serialled walnut dowel into the riser. An unannounced inspector then presses a catalogued marble paving tile against the still-damp dowel so the terrace soil, growth-ring serial, and tile vein map lock into one rubbing. A reused booking, borrowed dowel, or pre-inked tile collides on the inspector's timestamp and vein fingerprint and is slashed as a single farm; an attacker must pay for N terrace dawns, N uniquely turned walnut dowels, and N live inspector rubbings.
